title: The ALMA Frontier Fields Survey. VI. Lensing-corrected 1.1 mm number counts in Abell 2744, MACSJ0416.1-2403, MACSJ1149.5+2223, Abell 370, and Abell S1063
question: Derive lensing-corrected 1.1 mm number counts down to flux densities fainter than 0.1 mJy towards five Hubble Frontier Fields galaxy clusters and determine their contribution to the extragalactic background light (EBL).

what.value: Photometric redshift probability distributions from HFF-DeepSpace catalog

evidence.quote: We restrict our photometric redshift search to those data providing full posterior probability distributions, i.e. the HFF-DeepSpace project.
(cite: Shipley2018) derived photometric redshifts using up to 22 filters in the wavelength range $0.2-8\,\mu\textmd{m}$ and the EAZY fitting code (cite: Brammer2008).

what.value: Spectroscopic redshifts from the GLASS survey using HST grism spectroscopy

evidence.quote: These include spectroscopic redshifts from the GLASS survey using grism spectroscopy at HST (cite: Treu2015), and photometric redshifts (including full probability distributions) derived in Paper II for our high-significance detections via spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting.

what.value: Spectroscopic redshift for A370-ID03 from VLT/MUSE

evidence.quote: A370-ID03 has a $z_{\textmd{spec}}=1.258$ (secure) counterpart within $\approx0.2\ensuremath{''}$ from (cite: Lagattuta2022) using MUSE at VLT.

what.value: Spectroscopic redshift for AS1063-ID04 from CLASH VLT/MUSE

evidence.quote: It also has a $z_{\textmd{spec}}=0.611$ (secure) counterpart within $\approx0.9\ensuremath{''}$ from CLASH using MUSE at VLT. We adopt the latter value for this work.

what.value: Planck and COBE/FIRAS Extragalactic Background Light (EBL) estimates at 263.14 GHz

evidence.quote: We compare our estimates to that by the Planck collaboration (using their best-fit extended halo model, see (cite: Ade2014)) and a recent determination based on COBE/FIRAS and Planck observations (cite: Odegard2019).

what.value: Public Frontier Fields gravitational lens models (Bradac v4/v4.1, Caminha v4, CATS v4/v4.1, Diego v4/v4.1, GLAFIC v4, Keeton v4, Sharon v4, Williams v4/v4.1)

evidence.quote: Table [\[tab_models\]](#tab_models) lists these models, together with the models considered for the two FF clusters introduced in this work; we adopt for use eight, nine, seven, nine, and nine lens models for A2744, MACSJ0416, MACSJ1149, A370, and AS1063, respectively.

recipe.goal: Source detection and extraction in ALMA 1.1 mm mosaics
recipe.method: Search for pixels with S/N >= 4.5 within the PB > 0.3 region and group pixels into individual sources using the DBSCAN algorithm.

recipe.goal: Measure integrated flux densities and sizes of detected sources
recipe.method: For high-significance (S/N >= 5) sources, fit elliptical Gaussians in the uv-plane using UVMCMCFIT. For low-significance (4.5 <= S/N < 5) sources, scale peak intensities using median size parameters from high-S/N sources and source injection simulations.
key_parameters: Peak-to-integrated flux ratios of 0.80 (A370) and 0.71 (AS1063) for 4.5 <= S/N < 5 sources
assumptions: Low-significance detections have observed effective radius r_eff,obs = 0.23'' and axial ratio q_obs = 0.58 (median of high-S/N sources)

recipe.method: Cross-match ALMA detections with spectroscopic (ALMA linescan, GLASS, VLT/MUSE, Gemini/GMOS) and photometric (HFF-DeepSpace EAZY posteriors, Paper II) catalogs; assign Gaussian redshift prior to unassociated sources.
key_parameters: Matching radius <= 0.5'' for photometric counterparts (up to ~1'' for spectroscopic), redshift quality parameter p_Delta_z ~ 1
assumptions: Gaussian redshift distribution z = 2 +/- 0.5 for sources without counterparts

recipe.goal: Estimate image-plane completeness, flux deboosting, and spurious source fractions
recipe.method: Perform image-plane source injection simulations to derive completeness as a function of flux and size, and flux deboosting as a function of S/N. Extract sources from 300 simulated noise maps per cluster to determine spurious fraction p_false(S/N).
key_parameters: 300 simulated noise maps per cluster; 10^4 simulated SIDES point sources for Eddington bias check
assumptions: Skip separate Eddington bias corrections since SIDES simulation flux enhancements match deboosting corrections

recipe.goal: Compute source-plane magnification maps and effective areas from lens models
recipe.method: Reproject surface mass density and shear maps from public v4/v4.1 lens models to ALMA resolution, deflect magnification and PB-corrected rms maps to the source plane over a redshift grid, and integrate pixels where S_demag,peak / sigma_demag >= 4.5.
key_parameters: Redshift grid z_min = 0.4 to z_max = 4 with step Delta z = 0.2; 8, 9, 7, 9, and 9 lens models for A2744, MACSJ0416, MACSJ1149, A370, and AS1063
assumptions: No magnification (mu = 1) for pixels missing in lens model maps; neglect differential magnification; flat LambdaCDM cosmology with H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7

recipe.goal: Derive lensing-corrected differential and cumulative number counts via Monte Carlo simulations
recipe.method: Run 1000 Monte Carlo realizations per lens model per cluster drawing observed fluxes, peak intensities, redshifts, and lens mass reconstructions, computing demagnified fluxes and summing weights X_i = (1 - p_false,i) / (C_i * A_eff,i). Combine by taking medians and adding 16th/84th percentile errors in quadrature with Gehrels Poisson uncertainties.
key_parameters: 1000 realizations per lens model per cluster field
assumptions: Modified black body with beta = 1.5, T_dust = 35 K, z = 2.5 when scaling literature counts from 850 um, 1.2 mm, and 1.3 mm to 1.1 mm

recipe.goal: Compute resolved and extrapolated Extragalactic Background Light (EBL) at 1.1 mm
recipe.method: Sum the integrated flux contribution across differential count bins in each Monte Carlo realization, and fit a double power-law function to non-zero bins of each realization to integrate down to S_lim = 0, 0.013, and 0.133 mJy.
key_parameters: Parameter bounds: N_0 = 10^3 - 10^6 mJy deg^-2, S_0 = 0.01 - 1 mJy, alpha = 0 - 5, beta = -1 to 1

answer_key.quantity: Total number of ALMA 1.1 mm detections (S/N >= 4.5) across 5 clusters

evidence.quote: We created a source catalog that includes ALMA $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ continuum detections around two new FF galaxy clusters, together with the sources previously detected around three FF galaxy clusters, making a total of 29 detected sources down to a $4.5\sigma$ significance.

answer_key.quantity: Total observed image-plane area across 5 clusters (PB > 0.3)

evidence.quote: Each cluster field covers an observed area of $\sim5.2\,\textmd{arcmin}^2$ ($\textmd{PB}>0.3$ region). The five clusters sum to a total image-plane area of $\sim26\,\textmd{arcmin}^2$.

answer_key.quantity: Empirical field-to-field cosmic variance down to 0.013 mJy

evidence.quote: First, we derive the field-to-field variance directly from our cumulative counts, computing the variance from the median counts per cluster field down to $0.013\,\textmd{mJy}$. Dividing its square root by the number of clusters and the corresponding median combined counts, we obtain a relative uncertainty of 17%.

answer_key.quantity: Resolved EBL contribution at 1.1 mm down to 0.013 mJy (direct summation)

evidence.quote: We find a median contribution of $14.3_{-7.4}^{+12.2}$ ($7.5_{-3.9}^{+6.4}$) $\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$ resolved in our demagnified sources at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ down to $0.013$ ($0.133$) $\textmd{mJy}$; here, uncertainties are computed from the 16th and 84th percentiles.

answer_key.quantity: Resolved EBL contribution at 1.1 mm down to 0.133 mJy (direct summation)

evidence.quote: We find a median contribution of $14.3_{-7.4}^{+12.2}$ ($7.5_{-3.9}^{+6.4}$) $\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$ resolved in our demagnified sources at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ down to $0.013$ ($0.133$) $\textmd{mJy}$; here, uncertainties are computed from the 16th and 84th percentiles.

answer_key.quantity: Double power-law fit parameter S_0 (turnover flux density)

evidence.quote: From these fits, we find median parameters and associated uncertainties (from 16th and 84th percentiles) of $N_0=2.7_{-1.7}^{+5.0}\times10^5\,\textmd{mJy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$, $S_0=3.6_{-2.3}^{+2.5}\times10^{-2}\,\textmd{mJy}$, $\alpha=2.8_{-0.8}^{+1.0}$, and $\beta=0.6_{-1.6}^{+0.4}$.

answer_key.quantity: Total extrapolated EBL at 1.1 mm (double power-law fit integrated down to S_lim = 0 mJy)

evidence.quote: Using Eq. [\[eq_dpl_ebl\]](#eq_dpl_ebl) with the parameters found for each realization and $S_{\textmd{lim}}=0\,\textmd{mJy}$, we estimate a median total EBL associated with $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ galaxies in the FFs of $21.2_{-9.6}^{+40.4}\,\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$.

score_reason: The ALMA project codes, public MAST lens model versions, source catalog (positions, peak and uv-fitted fluxes, sizes, and redshifts), and final number count tables are thoroughly documented. However, full end-to-end reproduction requires custom Monte Carlo lensing simulation scripts that are not released, reduction details deferred to Paper I/III/IV, and unstated DBSCAN and noise-simulation parameters.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA datasets (2013.1.00999.S, 2015.1.01425.S, 2017.1.01219.S) and MAST Frontier Fields lens models are public, and the main results (source catalog fluxes/sizes, lensing-corrected differential/cumulative number counts, and EBL contributions) are concrete numeric benchmarks.
